reviewer: Codex, personal complete-final-answer read; no paid judge
primary_route: Low-ATP angular stepping and load/drag energetics with parallel bulk ATPase and inferred per-step stoichiometry.

checks.reason: No explicit proposal to consult/check prior primary Methods or a validated protocol for detailed pre-execution conditions and transfer. Recording unknown settings and developing an assay locally do not satisfy this distinct requirement.

The core immobilization/shaft attachment, solution chemistry (including nucleotide/free-magnesium conditions), recording settings and load manipulation lack an executable quantitative workflow or a concrete calibration-to-setting procedure. Lists of parameters to select later are insufficient.

Synthetic validation uses implanted steps but does not require a continuous/no-step false-positive challenge or quantitative recovery/false-call gates; stationary noise alone does not validate stepping. The inactive-enzyme Brownian drag reference also needs a free-pivot/confinement check before applying D=kT/drag.

Correct independent-preparation/chamber/molecule hierarchy is present, but the sample-size pilot does not specify a quantitative precision/power target linked to meaningful effect and between-preparation variance.

The population denominator is restricted to rotating filaments, and acquisition quotas favor molecules with many completed turns without retaining initially eligible inactive/irregular complexes as outcomes.
Primary estimands and hierarchical/held-out comparisons are present, but exact model assumptions/diagnostics and multiplicity control for the several primary load/coupling/event tests are incomplete.
Pilot separation and troubleshooting are described, but technical changes do not explicitly trigger a revised freeze and fresh independent confirmatory data under a defined change-control policy.

The positive decision asserts one turnover per 120-degree step and quantified efficiency from ensemble congruence and ATP-dependent waits despite acknowledged unknown contributing active fraction. A constant binding-limited rate does not count hydrolysis per event; efficiency per ATP is conditional on unverified stoichiometry. This is a critical failure of the proposed joint energetic inference, not of the stepping question.
No complete preserved raw-movie/trace/chemistry calibration manifest with molecule identifiers and exact analysis versions/settings is specified.

checks.quote: rotation is biased diffusion rather than fixed-ratio stepping
checks.reason: Brownian/ratchet force generation and tight stoichiometric stepping are not mutually exclusive. The stated loose-versus-biased-diffusion mechanism decision conflates force-generation class with coupling stoichiometry; a separate fluctuation/kinetic discrimination is needed.

The opening reported-inference chain upgrades the sparse observation to continuous unidirectional hydrolysis-driven motion. Continuity and chemical-energy conversion details are precisely unresolved by this packet; later caution does not make them observed facts.

explanation_reason: Hits the historical topics and offers useful load/ATP experiments, but an unverified ATP-per-step premise makes the proposed efficiency conclusion non-identifying; several operational safeguards are also missing.
historical_match_reason: Question/mechanism/intervention/readouts include stepping, ATP/load discrimination, drag-derived work and condition-specific chemical free energy. However, the joint positive conclusion assigns one ATP per 120-degree step from bulk rate matching with unknown active fraction and ATP-dependent waiting. Its own caveat concedes stoichiometry is assumed. That critical coupling-to-efficiency inference prevents a qualified predicted-outcome hit; merely naming 120 degrees does not rescue it.
